title: Port continuous batcher to event-strand runtime and shrink KV cache ownership
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: The continuous-batcher currently runs on a mix of threadpool-based executors and ad-hoc worker threads. This has resulted in subtle contention on the global scheduler lock, complicated shutdown semantics, and an expansive KV cache ownership surface that creates transient memory spikes and makes GC/eviction tricky. Goal: Port the continuous-batcher core to the event-strand (single-threaded strand per shard) runtime, reduce shared mutable KV ownership to a borrow/lease API, and introduce explicit memory accounting for KV entries. Success criteria: 1) 99th percentile tail latency reduction for short-sequence workloads (<= 64 tokens) by >= 15% under p95 load; 2) steady-state KV resident memory decrease by >= 20% for multi-tenant benchmarks; 3) simplified shutdown path with no >1s blocking ops on critical thread. Scope: - Introduce strand executor glue (non-invasive): adapter layer that runs batch state machines on event-strands; - Implement KVCacher V2 with borrow/lease semantics and compact ownership map; - Replace global scheduler lock with per-shard rendezvous and light-weight admission counters; - Add memory-usage accounting hooks exposed to telemetry for per-tenant dashboards; - Provide compatibility shim so Dedicated and Hosted runtimes can toggle the new path via feature flag. Risks & mitigations: - Behavioral regressions under high-concurrency: add load-tests and shadow path for 2 weeks before rollout. - Eviction correctness: introduce property-based tests and a KV consistency monitor in Console. Rollout plan: feature-flagged Canary (10% of Hosted), monitor latency/memory/error-rate for 7 days, expand to Dedicated after SLA smoke tests. Rollback: flip feature flag to revert to existing batcher. Artifacts: design doc -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Event-Strand-Design, benchmark harness -> gs://redwood-bench/continuous-batcher/2026-03, PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8453.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Initial spike: prototype an event-strand adapter and benchmark against threadpool baseline. Short-sequence QPS test shows ~9% tail-latency gain in a single-shard microbenchmark. — Miguel

2026-03-04 - Design review notes from Lena Martinez: 1) clarify lease lifetimes in KVCacher V2, 2) prefer explicit eviction fencing in cross-shard handoff, 3) add rollout gating for Dedicated. Lena left inline comments in the Confluence doc.

2026-03-06 - Dependency upgrade proposal: bump internal executor shim to v2.3 (adds strand APIs) and upgrade tracing lib for non-blocking span flush. Security review not required per initial triage. — Aisha

2026-03-08 - Implemented borrow/lease API and unit tests. Observed a memory reduction of ~22% in local multi-tenant replay tests and 12% throughput improvement under mixed short/long workloads. Created draft PR: #8453. — Miguel

2026-03-09 - Code review (Noah Chen): requested clearer invariants around lease expiration and stronger assertions in hotpath to avoid silent stale reads. Filed follow-up TODOs in code and added a lightweight consistency checker in telemetry.

2026-03-11 - Integration test: run canary against dedicated-sim cluster. Found a race in shutdown when a strand tries to steal work from a draining shard; added a draining flag and handshake protocol. Re-ran tests: no regressions observed.

2026-03-12 - PM check-in (Priya Desai): align with Console team to surface per-tenant memory metrics; added 'kvcache.lease.active' metric to the telemetry contract. Preparing canary rollout ticket and runbook.
notes: This ticket intentionally keeps the public API stable. The new borrow/lease semantics are internal to the runtime; user-facing model pinning and rollouts are unaffected. We'll coordinate with Solutions to ensure no churn for existing Dedicated customers during the rollout.
